description: We are just normal people participating in the hackathon
summary: SEIS & Apollo Seismic Command is an interactive hardware-in-the-loop space outpost simulator designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Developed to address resource-constrained lunar and Martian base management, our solution bridges real-world planetary seismology with strategic survival gameplay. The system integrates a physical piezoelectric seismic station connected to an ESP32 microcontroller, streaming real-time telemetry via USB to a Python-based mission control dashboard. To mimic NASA missions like Apollo and InSight, the firmware executes discrete-time digital signal processing algorithms to filter environmental noise and detect moonquakes or marsquakes. Players act as outpost commanders, striving to collect $50,000 in Science Funds while managing vital life-support resources—Habitat Integrity, Oxygen Reserves, and Reactor Power—against escalating seismic hazards and periodic meteorite swarms.
details:
1. WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS: SEIS & Apollo Seismic Command is an interactive hardware-in-the-loop space outpost simulator. A physical piezoelectric sensor connected to an ESP32 captures real vibrations, applies discrete-time digital signal processing (DSP) to filter electrical noise, and streams live seismic waves via USB Serial to a Python mission control interface. Players must reach $50,000 in Science Funds by scanning tremors while preventing Habitat Integrity, Oxygen Reserve, and Reactor Power from hitting 0%. 2. BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT: Our project transforms complex aerospace concepts—planetary seismology, signal filtering, and life-support engineering—into an accessible, hands-on STEM learning experience inspired by NASA's Apollo and Mars InSight (SEIS) missions. 3. TOOLS, LANGUAGES, HARDWARE & SOFTWARE: - Hardware: ESP32 microcontroller (12-bit ADC), piezoelectric sensor with proof mass, PWM buzzer, and status LEDs on a PCB. - Software & Languages: MicroPython (firmware), Python 3, Tkinter (GUI), and PySerial. 4. CREATIVITY & FACTORS CONSIDERED: Instead of a keyboard-only game, we built a physical-digital survival loop where real tremors drive the economy. Our team considered real sensor noise floors, thermal baseline drift, and a high-risk/high-reward resource balance against marsquakes and meteorite swarms.

Note on SI/AI Use: AI assistant tools (LLMs) were used for code debugging, UI translation to English, and text editing. All hardware design, ESP32 assembly, and discrete-time DSP implementation were developed by the team.
